content_html:
The SSH client for AI agents and humans. Connect by name. Reuse authenticated SSH connections. Keep secrets local.

Latest release: Corv v1.1 | Complete changelog

AI agents don't use SSH the way humans do. Raw SSH requires the calling workflow to manage connection details, authentication configuration, prompts, and terminal output. Independent invocations also repeat connection setup unless OpenSSH multiplexing is configured, while long-running work commonly needs tmux, nohup, or custom scripts.

Corv is built for agent-driven infrastructure. It lets agents connect by name, execute commands without exposing passwords or private keys, receive structured JSON output, reuse a warm authenticated connection, and detach and resume long-running jobs. Humans use the same saved connection profiles through an interactive terminal UI.

Install

Linux / macOS

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/khalid-src/corv-client/main/install.sh | sh

Windows (PowerShell)

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/khalid-src/corv-client/main/install.ps1 | iex

With Go

go install github.com/khalid-src/corv-client/cmd/corv@latest

Update or remove

corv update      # download and install the latest release (checksum-verified)
corv uninstall   # remove corv; add --purge to also delete saved connections

corv update only runs when you run it - Corv never updates itself in the background.

Usage

Manage connections interactively:

corv

The terminal interface supports keyboard and mouse navigation to add, edit, import from ~/.ssh/config, and connect. Connections can also be managed from the command line:

corv add prod-api deploy@api.example.com                    # prompts for a password if needed
corv add prod-api deploy@api.example.com --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
corv add prod-db dbadmin@db.example.com --jump ops@bastion.example.com
corv import                                          # import hosts from ~/.ssh/config
corv list
corv test prod-api                                   # diagnose connection stages
corv status                                          # show warm connections and active runs
corv rm prod-api

corv test <name> opens and immediately closes a one-off SSH connection. It checks resolution, TCP reachability, bastion routing, the SSH handshake, host-key trust, and authentication without running a remote command. Add --json for structured diagnostics. Raw targets and addresses require --full. corv status reports the connections the local broker currently holds, hides targets unless --full is specified, and does not start a stopped broker.

Hosts behind one or more bastions are reached with --jump (OpenSSH -J syntax: user@host1,user@host2). Jump hosts authenticate with ssh-agent or your keys; the target uses the connection's own credentials.

corv add reads any password without echo and stores it in the local encrypted vault; it is never passed as an argument.

corv vault reset clears stored SSH passwords and private-key passphrases while keeping saved connections. It asks for confirmation and stops the local broker before changing state. If the encrypted connection store cannot be opened, Corv cannot determine whether its key is unavailable or the config file is damaged; it refuses a normal reset. corv vault reset --all explicitly removes the local connection store, vault data, backend marker, and Corv-managed local key file. Externally provisioned OS keychain entries are not removed.

Connect interactively:

corv prod-api

Run a command non-interactively (the agent path):

corv prod-api -- uname -a
corv prod-api --json -- df -h             # structured output for tools
corv prod-api -- ./deploy.sh
echo 'cd /app && run "$X" | grep foo' | corv prod-api --json --stdin
corv prod-api --json --stdin < script.sh

A typical agent instruction such as "check disk usage on prod-api" requires only corv prod-api -- df -h.

Command handling after -- is designed to do what you mean:

  • a single argument is treated as a remote shell command line and run as-is, like ssh host "cmd" - e.g. corv srv -- "cd /app && make";
  • multiple arguments are passed as a preserved argument vector, each shell-quoted so the remote cannot re-split them - e.g. corv srv -- sh -lc "cd /app && make".

This preserves argument boundaries for callers that construct command vectors.

For complex shell text, nested quotes, or multi-line scripts, use an stdin mode. --stdin-base64 is the cross-shell-safe option because only ASCII base64 passes through the local pipe.

Windows / PowerShell

PowerShell can mangle quoting and pipe encoding, so encode a non-trivial remote command as UTF-8 base64 and send it with --stdin-base64:

$b64=[Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes(@'
set -eu
cd /srv/app && ./deploy.sh
'@)); $b64 | corv prod-api --json --stdin-base64

Only ASCII base64 crosses the pipe, so the command arrives unchanged - quoting and any non-ASCII text survive intact. A simple exact argument vector can still use -- <command>.

Long commands are detached on the server automatically. If a command is still running after the broker's wait window, Corv returns the new bounded output, the run id, and exit code 75. Re-run the exact same command to watch the next delta; it attaches to the existing remote job and does not start a second copy. When the job finishes, Corv retains up to 20 MiB locally and removes the remote temporary files. If a log is larger, Corv keeps its first 4 MiB and its final section with an omission marker between them, so late failures are not lost. truncated: true in corv output --json reports this case:

corv prod-api -- ./long-install.sh
corv output <run-id> [pattern]         # bounded status/output view
# The byte-identical original command can also reattach while it is running.

CORV_WAIT controls how long the broker waits before returning a running response. It accepts bare seconds (CORV_WAIT=30) or a Go duration (CORV_WAIT=500ms, CORV_WAIT=2m) and is read from the environment of each corv invocation, so it takes effect immediately without restarting the broker. corv output <run-id> checks an unfinished detached run and finalizes it automatically once the remote exit status exists. Remote temp files are cleaned on finalization. The startup sweep removes completed remote remnants older than 24 hours; it never deletes a run without an exit status because age alone cannot distinguish an abandoned run from a silent live process. Saved local run logs and their metadata are retained for 24 hours and removed on broker startup.

corv output exits 75 while a run is active, with the remote exit code when it completes, and 1 for a Corv retrieval error. The process exit code and JSON exit_code field use the same value.

All agent-facing output is bounded. Completed responses and corv output return a middle-out view of roughly 32 KiB; running responses use a smaller budget. Pass a pattern to corv output to select relevant lines before that budget is applied. JSON responses report original_bytes, saved_bytes, returned_bytes, truncated (the retained log omitted bytes), and output_truncated (the returned view was bounded) when applicable.

Remote command execution requires a POSIX shell and standard Unix command-line tools. Windows OpenSSH servers are not supported as remote execution targets.

Use with AI agents

Corv is built for AI coding agents (Claude, Codex, and others). Ready-to-use agent instructions live in integrations/:

  • Claude / Claude Code - copy integrations/claude/corv-ssh into ~/.claude/skills/ (or a project's .claude/skills/).
  • Codex - copy integrations/codex/AGENTS.md into your project.

The agent then runs commands by name and reads structured output:

corv <name> --json -- <command>

For non-trivial scripts or heavily quoted commands, agents should send the remote command as UTF-8 base64:

$b64=[Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes(@'
set -eu
cd /srv/app && ./deploy.sh
'@)); $b64 | corv <name> --json --stdin-base64

Agents should not run corv list --full, corv doctor --full, corv test <name> --full, or corv status --full unless the user explicitly asks; those modes show local connection details. Never put passwords, private keys, API tokens, bootstrap tokens, bearer tokens, or other secrets on the command line. Corv command history records command lines.

See integrations/README.md for details.

Connection reuse

A local broker process holds one authenticated SSH connection per saved profile. Each corv <name> -- <cmd> runs as a new channel over the held connection, so the connection and authentication cost is paid once rather than on every command. This behaviour is identical on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

OpenSSH can also reuse connections on Unix through ControlMaster and a control socket. Corv provides the same warm-connection model through its local broker so agent workflows behave consistently on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

The broker starts automatically on first use, exits after 15 minutes idle, and installs nothing on the server. It manages SSH connections only; it does not allocate a local pseudo-terminal, parse shell output, or maintain remote shell state. A held connection can be dropped explicitly:

corv disconnect prod-api

Scope and limitations:

  • This is connection reuse, not remote session persistence. Each command runs in its own shell with its own exit code; shell state such as the working directory does not carry between commands (combine them in a single command when required, e.g. cd /app && make).
  • Because the broker is local, a held connection does not survive the local machine sleeping or a network interruption. Persistence across those events requires remote support, which Corv does not depend on by design.

Interactive sessions open a dedicated connection and proxy the remote pseudo-terminal to the local terminal, so no local pseudo-terminal is required on any platform.

Output processing

Corv normalises command output for programmatic consumers:

  • progress bars and other carriage-return redraws are collapsed to their final state rather than reproduced as thousands of lines;
  • ANSI control sequences, including colour, are removed;
  • a command's stdout and stderr are captured together, interleaved in the order they were written, and returned in stdout; with --json, the stderr field carries Corv-level errors (e.g. transport failures), not the remote command's own stderr;
  • completed and running responses use fixed byte budgets and preserve the beginning and end with a ... N line(s) hidden ... marker; corv output <run-id> [pattern] queries the retained log through the same bounded presentation contract;
  • failures are classified (auth_failed, unknown_host, unknown_connection, bad_request, local_error, unreachable, host_key, timeout, disconnected, resource_exhausted, ssh_error), and the remote exit code is propagated as the process exit code.

Security model

Corv runs entirely on the client and implements SSH through the maintained Go SSH library (golang.org/x/crypto/ssh).

  • Nothing is installed on the destination server.
  • Connection profiles are encrypted at rest with the same local vault key used for stored credentials, so the connection file does not expose hosts, users, or paths in plaintext (corv list is the way to view them).
  • Passwords and key passphrases are stored in a local encrypted vault. The vault key is protected by DPAPI on Windows; on macOS and Linux Corv reads a provisioned Keychain / Secret Service key when present (it never auto-creates one) and otherwise uses a 0600 key file, the default. Stored secrets are read only by the local broker and sent over the authenticated SSH connection; they do not appear on a command line, in logs, or in command output. Key-based authentication or ssh-agent is recommended.
  • Audit logs and saved run logs are local and can contain the command text or remote output an operator asked Corv to run. Never put passwords, private keys, API tokens, bootstrap tokens, bearer tokens, or other secrets on the command line; command history records command lines.
  • Authentication is attempted in order: configured identity file, ssh-agent (via SSH_AUTH_SOCK on Unix, the openssh-ssh-agent named pipe on Windows), default ~/.ssh keys, then password.
  • Bastion (ProxyJump) hops are host-key verified individually and can authenticate with ssh-agent, default keys, a per-hop identity file, or a password/passphrase sourced from a saved profile.
  • Host keys are verified against ~/.ssh/known_hosts. An unknown host is rejected unless approved interactively; the broker never accepts unknown hosts automatically. A changed host key is always rejected.
  • The broker uses OS-permissioned local IPC (Unix socket or Windows named pipe) plus an endpoint token for defense in depth.

Architecture

Corv is composed of small, independent modules so that the SSH backend or the output processor can be replaced without affecting the rest:

Package Responsibility
internal/profile connection definitions, storage, ~/.ssh/config import
internal/vault local encrypted secret store and key backends
internal/sshconn SSH transport (x/crypto/ssh): dial, auth, exec, shell
internal/broker resident process holding one connection per profile
internal/output output processor (collapse, strip, bound)
internal/audit local command history
internal/tui interactive terminal UI (Bubble Tea)
internal/cli command-line routing
internal/statelock cross-process lock serialising local state writes
internal/atomicfile crash-safe atomic file writes
internal/paths on-disk file locations

Development

go build ./...
go vet ./...
go test ./...

The Makefile also provides make build and make build-all on systems with make. Corv targets Go 1.25+ with automatic toolchain selection; CI and release builds use the version pinned in go.mod on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

blocks.html_en: CORV_WAIT controls how long the broker waits before returning a running response. It accepts bare seconds (CORV_WAIT=30) or a Go duration (CORV_WAIT=500ms, CORV_WAIT=2m) and is read from the environment of each corv invocation, so it takes effect immediately without restarting the broker. corv output <run-id> checks an unfinished detached run and finalizes it automatically once the remote exit status exists. Remote temp files are cleaned on finalization. The startup sweep removes completed remote remnants older than 24 hours; it never deletes a run without an exit status because age alone cannot distinguish an abandoned run from a silent live process. content_html_zh:
适用于 AI 代理和人类的 SSH 客户端。 按名称连接。 重用经过身份验证的 SSH 连接。 保守秘密。

最新版本：Corv v1.1 |完整的变更日志

AI 代理不像人类那样使用 SSH。 原始 SSH 需要调用工作流程来管理连接详细信息、身份验证配置、提示和终端输出。 独立调用也会重复连接设置，除非配置了 OpenSSH 多路复用，而长时间运行的工作通常需要 tmux、nohup 或自定义脚本。

Corv 是为代理驱动的基础设施而构建的。 它允许代理按名称连接、在不暴露密码或私钥的情况下执行命令、接收结构化 JSON 输出、重用经过身份验证的热连接以及分离和恢复长时间运行的作业。 人们通过交互式终端 UI 使用相同的已保存连接配置文件。

安装

Linux / macOS

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/khalid-src/corv-client/main/install.sh | sh

Windows（PowerShell）

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/khalid-src/corv-client/main/install.ps1 | iex

随走

go install github.com/khalid-src/corv-client/cmd/corv@latest

更新或删除

corv update      # download and install the latest release (checksum-verified)
corv uninstall   # remove corv; add --purge to also delete saved connections

corv update 仅在您运行时运行 - Corv 永远不会在后台更新自身。

Usage

交互式管理连接：

corv

终端界面支持键盘和鼠标导航来添加、编辑、从 ~/.ssh/config 导入和连接。 还可以从命令行管理连接：

corv add prod-api deploy@api.example.com                    # prompts for a password if needed
corv add prod-api deploy@api.example.com --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
corv add prod-db dbadmin@db.example.com --jump ops@bastion.example.com
corv import                                          # import hosts from ~/.ssh/config
corv list
corv test prod-api                                   # diagnose connection stages
corv status                                          # show warm connections and active runs
corv rm prod-api

corv test <name> 打开并立即关闭一次性 SSH 连接。 它可以检查分辨率、TCP 可达性、堡垒路由、SSH 握手、主机密钥信任和身份验证，而无需运行远程命令。 添加 --json 以进行结构化诊断。 原始目标和地址需要 --full。 corv status 报告本地代理当前持有的连接，隐藏目标（除非指定 --full），并且不会启动已停止的代理。

使用 --jump 可以到达一个或多个堡垒后面的主机（OpenSSH -J 语法：user@host1,user@host2）。 跳转主机使用 ssh-agent 或您的密钥进行身份验证；目标使用连接自己的凭据。

corv add 读取任何密码而不回显并将其存储在本地加密保管库中；它永远不会作为参数传递。

corvVault Reset 清除存储的 SSH 密码和私钥密码，同时保留保存的连接。 它要求确认并在更改状态之前停止本地代理。 如果加密连接存储无法打开，Corv无法确定其密钥是否不可用或配置文件已损坏；它拒绝正常重置。 corvVault Reset --all 显式删除本地连接存储、Vault 数据、后端标记和 Corv 管理的本地密钥文件。 外部配置的操作系统钥匙串条目不会被删除。

交互连接：

corv prod-api

以非交互方式运行命令（代理路径）：

corv prod-api -- uname -a
corv prod-api --json -- df -h             # structured output for tools
corv prod-api -- ./deploy.sh
echo 'cd /app && run "$X" | grep foo' | corv prod-api --json --stdin
corv prod-api --json --stdin < script.sh

典型的代理指令（例如“检查 prod-api 上的磁盘使用情况”）仅需要 corv prod-api -- df -h。

-- 之后的命令处理旨在执行您的意思：

  • 单个参数被视为远程 shell 命令行并按原样运行，如 ssh 主机“cmd” - 例如corv srv --“cd /app && make”;
  • 多个参数作为保留的参数向量传递，每个参数都用 shell 引用，因此远程无法重新分割它们 - 例如corv srv -- sh -lc“cd /app && make”。

这为构造命令向量的调用者保留了参数边界。

对于复杂的 shell 文本、嵌套引号或多行脚本，请使用 stdin 模式。 --stdin-base64 是跨 shell 安全选项，因为只有 ASCII base64 通过本地管道。

Windows / PowerShell

PowerShell 可以破坏引用和管道编码，因此将重要的远程命令编码为 UTF-8 base64 并使用 --stdin-base64 发送：

$b64=[Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes(@'
set -eu
cd /srv/app && ./deploy.sh
'@)); $b64 | corv prod-api --json --stdin-base64

只有 ASCII base64 穿过管道，因此命令到达时不会发生变化 - 引用和任何非 ASCII 文本都会完好无损。 一个简单的精确参数向量仍然可以使用--<command>。

长命令会在服务器上自动分离。 如果命令在代理的等待窗口之后仍在运行，Corv 将返回新的有界输出、运行 ID 和退出代码 75。 重新运行完全相同的命令来观察下一个增量；它附加到现有的远程作业并且不会启动第二个副本。 作业完成后，Corv 在本地保留最多 20 MiB 并删除远程临时文件。 如果日志较大，Corv 会保留其前 4 MiB 和最后部分，并在它们之间有一个省略标记，因此后期故障不会丢失。 corv 输出 --json 中的 truncated: true 报告了这种情况：

corv prod-api -- ./long-install.sh
corv output <run-id> [pattern]         # bounded status/output view
# The byte-identical original command can also reattach while it is running.

CORV_WAIT 控制代理在返回运行响应之前等待的时间。 它接受裸秒（CORV_WAIT = 30）或Go持续时间（CORV_WAIT = 500ms，CORV_WAIT = 2m），并从每次corv调用的环境中读取，因此它会立即生效，而无需重新启动代理。 corv 输出 <run-id> 检查未完成的分离运行，并在远程退出状态存在时自动完成它。 远程临时文件在完成时被清除。 启动扫描会删除超过 24 小时的已完成远程残留；它永远不会删除没有退出状态的运行，因为仅年龄无法区分放弃的运行和静默的实时进程。 保存的本地运行日志及其元数据将保留 24 小时，并在代理启动时删除。

当运行处于活动状态时，corv 输出退出 75，完成时显示远程退出代码，1 表示 Corv 检索错误。 进程退出代码和 JSON exit_code 字段使用相同的值。

所有面向代理的输出都是有限的。 完成的响应和 corv 输出返回大约 32 KiB 的中出视图；运行响应使用较小的预算。 将模式传递给 corv 输出以在应用预算之前选择相关行。 JSON 响应在适用时报告original_bytes、saved_bytes、returned_bytes、truncated（保留的日志省略字节）和output_truncated（返回的视图有界）。

远程命令执行需要 POSIX shell 和标准 Unix 命令行工具。 不支持将 Windows OpenSSH 服务器作为远程执行目标。

与 AI 代理一起使用

Corv 是为 AI 编码代理（Claude、Codex 等）构建的。 即用型代理指令位于集成/中：

  • Claude / Claude 代码 - 将 Integrations/claude/corv-ssh 复制到 ~/.claude/skills/ （或项目的 .claude/skills/）。
  • Codex - 将 Integrations/codex/AGENTS.md 复制到您的项目中。

然后，代理按名称运行命令并读取结构化输出：

corv <name> --json -- <command>

对于重要的脚本或大量引用的命令，代理应以 UTF-8 base64 形式发送远程命令：

$b64=[Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes(@'
set -eu
cd /srv/app && ./deploy.sh
'@)); $b64 | corv <name> --json --stdin-base64

除非用户明确要求，代理不应运行 corv list --full、corv doctor --full、corv test <name> --full 或 corv status --full；这些模式显示本地连接详细信息。 切勿将密码、私钥、API 令牌、引导令牌、不记名令牌或其他机密放在命令行上。 Corv 命令历史记录记录命令行。

有关详细信息，请参阅integrations/README.md。

连接复用

本地代理进程为每个保存的配置文件保留一个经过身份验证的 SSH 连接。 每个 corv <name> -- <cmd> 作为新通道通过保持的连接运行，因此连接和身份验证成本只需支付一次，而不是针对每个命令支付。 此行为在 Linux、macOS 和 Windows 上是相同的。

OpenSSH 还可以通过 ControlMaster 和控制套接字重用 Unix 上的连接。 Corv 通过其本地代理提供相同的热连接模型，因此代理工作流程在 Windows、macOS 和 Linux 上表现一致。

代理在首次使用时自动启动，闲置 15 分钟后退出，并且不会在服务器上安装任何内容。 它仅管理 SSH 连接；它不分配本地伪终端、解析 shell 输出或维护远程 shell 状态。 可以显式删除保持的连接：

corv disconnect prod-api

范围和限制：

  • 这是连接重用，而不是远程会话持久性。 每个命令都在自己的 shell 中运行，并具有自己的退出代码； shell 状态（例如工作目录）不在命令之间携带（需要时将它们组合在单个命令中，例如 cd /app && make）。
  • 由于代理是本地的，因此保持的连接无法在本地计算机休眠或网络中断时继续存在。 这些事件的持久性需要远程支持，而 Corv 在设计上并不依赖远程支持。

交互式会话打开专用连接，并将远程伪终端代理到本地终端，因此在任何平台上都不需要本地伪终端。

输出处理

Corv 为编程消费者标准化命令输出：

  • 进度条和其他回车重画会折叠到最终状态，而不是复制为数千行；
  • 删除了 ANSI 控制序列，包括颜色；
  • 命令的 stdout 和 stderr 被一起捕获，按照它们的写入顺序交错，并在 stdout 中返回；使用 --json 时，stderr 字段携带 Corv 级别的错误（例如传输失败），而不是远程命令自己的 stderr；
  • 已完成和正在运行的响应使用固定字节预算并保留开头和结尾...... N 行隐藏... 标记； corv output <run-id> [pattern] 通过相同的有界表示合约查询保留的日志；
  • 失败被分类（auth_failed、unknown_host、unknown_connection、bad_request、local_error、unreachable、host_key、timeout、disconnected、resource_exhausted、ssh_error），并且远程退出代码作为进程退出代码传播。

安全模型

Corv 完全运行在客户端上，并通过维护的 Go SSH 库 (golang.org/x/crypto/ssh) 实现 SSH。

  • 目标服务器上未安装任何内容。
  • 连接配置文件使用用于存储凭据的相同本地保管库密钥进行静态加密，因此连接文件不会以明文形式公开主机、用户或路径（corv 列表是查看它们的方式）。
  • 密码和密钥密码存储在本地加密保管库中。 保管库密钥在 Windows 上受 DPAPI 保护；在 macOS 和 Linux 上，Corv 会读取已配置的钥匙串/秘密服务密钥（它从不自动创建），否则使用 0600 密钥文件（默认值）。 存储的秘密只能由本地代理读取并通过经过身份验证的 SSH 连接发送；它们不会出现在命令行、日志或命令输出中。 建议使用基于密钥的身份验证或 ssh-agent。
  • 审核日志和保存的运行日志位于本地，可以包含操作员要求 Corv 运行的命令文本或远程输出。 切勿将密码、私钥、API 令牌、引导令牌、不记名令牌或其他机密放在命令行上；命令历史记录记录命令行。
  • 尝试按顺序进行身份验证：配置的身份文件、ssh-agent（在 Unix 上通过 SSH_AUTH_SOCK，在 Windows 上通过 openssh-ssh-agent 命名管道）、默认 ~/.ssh 密钥，然后是密码。
  • Bastion (ProxyJump) 跃点是单独验证的主机密钥，并且可以使用 ssh-agent、默认密钥、每跳身份文件或来自已保存配置文件的密码/密码进行身份验证。
  • 主机密钥根据 ~/.ssh/known_hosts 进行验证。 除非交互批准，否则未知主机将被拒绝；代理永远不会自动接受未知主机。 更改的主机密钥始终会被拒绝。
  • 代理使用操作系统许可的本地 IPC（Unix 套接字或 Windows 命名管道）以及端点令牌进行深度防御。

建筑学

Corv 由小型独立模块组成，因此可以更换 SSH 后端或输出处理器而不影响其余部分：

包裹 责任
内部/轮廓 连接定义、存储、~/.ssh/config 导入
内部/金库 本地加密秘密存储和密钥后端
内部/sshconn SSH 传输 (x/crypto/ssh)：拨号、身份验证、执行、shell
内部/经纪人 每个配置文件持有一个连接的常驻进程
内部/输出 输出处理器（折叠、剥离、绑定）
内部/审计 本地命令历史记录
内部/tui 交互终端UI（珍珠奶茶）
内部/cli 命令行路由
内部/状态锁 跨进程锁序列化本地状态写入
内部/原子文件 崩溃安全原子文件写入
内部/路径 磁盘上的文件位置

发展

go build ./...
go vet ./...
go test ./...

Makefile 还提供了在带有 make 的系统上进行 make build 和 make build-all 的功能。 Corv 的目标是 Go 1.25+，具有自动工具链选择功能； CI 和发布版本使用 Linux、macOS 和 Windows 上 go.mod 中固定的版本。
